# Assessment — #435: Guardian: mTLS adapter auth + keep authn/authz seams generic (public ships Basic only)

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **M**._

## Current state (already merged)

Roughly two-thirds of this issue is already merged. (1) Generic authn seam: packages/guardian/src/auth.ts defines the pluggable AuthStrategy interface with setAuthStrategy/getAuthStrategy/resetAuthStrategy and an async-capable authenticate(req, expectedKind) (auth.ts:70-125); the built-in basicTokenAuthStrategy implements the Basic channelId:channelSecret -> AuthenticatedPrincipal model against the sqlite principal store with constant-time sha256 compare and a bounded principal cache. (2) Policy seam: packages/guardian/src/policy.ts defines PolicyProvider/PolicyRequest/PolicyDecision keyed on the generic principal id/kind, with allowAllPolicy as the shipped default; it IS consulted in the gate — proxy.ts:212-244 runs 'Gate 2b: pluggable authorization policy' before allowlist/ownership/moderation, failing closed (403 forbidden_policy) on provider errors, covered by proxy-policy.test.ts. (3) Library composition surface: packages/guardian/src/index.ts exports the seams plus createGuardian()/startGuardian() builder and the transport registry (transport.ts); server.ts only boots under import.meta.main; CHANGELOG Unreleased documents all of this (lines 40-58, 71-75). (4) Basic policy, static admin/MCP bearer tokens (GUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE / GUARDIAN_MCP_TOKEN_FILE, admin.ts + portals.compose.yml:127-128), and the principal registry (state-db.ts, bun:sqlite, kinds 'portal'|'direct' — the #433 store) are all in place and unchanged, matching the 'public ships Basic only' scope. WHAT DOES NOT EXIST: the mTLS adapter transport identity — the one piece this issue uniquely owns. There is zero TLS anywhere in guardian or the stack: no tls/cert matches in packages/guardian/src; all three listeners are plain-HTTP Bun.serve (server.ts:265-276); issue #557 independently confirms 'no TLS anywhere in the stack'. No mTLS strategy, no CA/cert config vars in config.ts, no cert secret mounts in packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml, no docs. Note the issue's 'channel_lan' terminology is stale — the adapter network was renamed portal_net in 0.12.0 (CHANGELOG.md:322), and the LAN-facing adapter surface is the direct listener (port 3830, GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS-gated, published at ${OP_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:3830 in portals.compose.yml:148).

## Remaining work

- [ ] Write a short design note (docs/technical/) fixing the mTLS termination approach for the direct listener (3830, the LAN adapter surface). Key constraint to resolve: Bun.serve's fetch handler does not expose the peer certificate, so choose between (a) handshake-level transport identity only — Bun.serve tls: { cert, key, ca, requestCert, rejectUnauthorized } where any cert signed by the operator's adapter CA passes and the Principal still comes from Basic auth (matches the issue's 'transport identity, not an identity provider' framing and is the smallest implementation), (b) a node:tls/node:https-based direct listener exposing getPeerCertificate() for cert-fingerprint -> principal mapping, or (c) deferring termination to #557's Caddy/Tailscale edge. Option (a) is recommended for public scope.
- [ ] Add opt-in TLS/mTLS config to packages/guardian/src/config.ts following the existing GUARDIAN_* file-based pattern: GUARDIAN_TLS_CERT_FILE, GUARDIAN_TLS_KEY_FILE, GUARDIAN_MTLS_CA_FILE (presence of the CA file enables requestCert+rejectUnauthorized). Default entirely off — when unset, listener construction in server.ts must be byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] Wire the TLS options into the direct listener in startGuardian (packages/guardian/src/server.ts:271-275) only; internal (8080, portal_net-only) and admin (3831, loopback) listeners stay plain HTTP. Include the mTLS enabled/disabled state in the 'started' reproducibility log line (server.ts:289-299) without ever logging key/cert material.
- [ ] If cert-identity mapping is chosen (option b): add an mtlsAuthStrategy in auth.ts (or a composed pre-step) mapping the verified client-cert SHA-256 fingerprint to a PrincipalRecord; extend state-db.ts with a nullable cert_fingerprint column + PRAGMA user_version migration, extend POST /admin/principals (admin.ts:61-66) to accept a fingerprint credential, and export the new pieces from index.ts. Skip this entire item under option (a).
- [ ] Compose/skeleton plumbing: add optional op_guardian_tls_cert / op_guardian_tls_key / op_guardian_mtls_ca secret mounts + env wiring to the guardian service in packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml. Secret names prefixed op_guardian_ already pass the secret-name authorization model (packages/lib/src/control-plane/secret-audit.ts:108-112) — verify with the existing secret-audit tests rather than new lib code.
- [ ] Tests: unit tests for config parsing (missing/partial cert files fail closed with a clear boot error); a subprocess integration test mirroring the Bun.spawn harness in server.test.ts:125 that generates a throwaway CA + client cert fixture, boots the guardian with the TLS env set, and asserts (1) a request with a CA-signed client cert succeeds, (2) no cert / wrong-CA cert is rejected at handshake, (3) with mTLS unset behavior is unchanged. If Bun.serve turns out not to support requestCert (spike first), this test is what proves the chosen fallback.
- [ ] Docs: update docs/technical/core-principles.md §Guardian-only ingress (line 58) and the port table (line 260) to describe the optional mTLS transport-identity layer; check scripts/security-posture-doc-drift.test.ts still passes (it asserts posture-prose/code agreement); add a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry. Use portal_net/adapter terminology, not the stale channel_lan.
- [ ] Confirm-and-close items already satisfied (verify, no code expected): AuthStrategy seam generic and async (auth.ts:70-125), PolicyProvider seam consulted fail-closed in the gate (proxy.ts:212-244), public guardian ships only Basic + allowAll (index.ts exports), admin/MCP bearer plumbing unchanged.

## Test strategy

Guardian tests are colocated bun:test files (packages/guardian/src/*.test.ts) run via `bun test --no-orphans` (packages/guardian/package.json 'test' script); the root suite runs them via `bun run test` which includes packages/guardian/ and scripts/. Test-first: (1) add src/tls-config.test.ts asserting config.ts fail-closed parsing of GUARDIAN_TLS_*/GUARDIAN_MTLS_CA_FILE (unset => disabled, partial => boot error); (2) add an mTLS integration test following the established subprocess pattern (server.test.ts:125 uses Bun.spawn(['bun','run','src/server.ts'], { env }) against ephemeral ports) — generate a self-signed CA + server cert + client cert fixture in beforeAll, boot with GUARDIAN_DIRECT_INGRESS=true and the TLS env, then assert handshake acceptance with the CA-signed client cert, rejection without one, and unchanged plain-HTTP behavior when TLS env is unset; (3) if the cert->principal mapping variant is chosen, add auth.ts unit tests mirroring auth.test.ts (principal cache, disabled principal, fingerprint mismatch) and a state-db migration test alongside state-db.test.ts; (4) run scripts/security-posture-doc-drift.test.ts after the core-principles.md edits. Verify seam regressions with the existing proxy-policy.test.ts and index.test.ts.

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #433 — the principal registry / guardian state store: an mTLS cert-fingerprint -> principal mapping (if chosen over handshake-only CA verification) adds a column + migration to the same bun:sqlite principals table #433 owns; the store already exists in packages/guardian/src/state-db.ts, so this is a coordination dependency, not a blocker.
- #557 — guardian edge TLS + CORS: both issues put TLS on guardian ingress. The termination-point decision must be shared — if #557 lands a Caddy/Tailscale front terminating TLS for remote clients, #435's mTLS on the direct listener must either terminate at that same front (client-cert verification forwarded) or bind a separate raw-TLS listener; #557's scope list explicitly says 'coordinate with #435'. CORS allowlist groundwork (GUARDIAN_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS, config.ts:52) has already landed.

## Risks

- Bun.serve may not expose client-certificate details (and possibly not requestCert/rejectUnauthorized) to the fetch handler — spike this first; if unsupported, the direct listener needs a node:https fallback under Bun's node-compat or the feature reduces to handshake-only CA verification. This is the single biggest unknown.
- Cert lifecycle UX: the issue ships no CA-management tooling; without a documented provisioning path (who mints the adapter CA and client certs, how they rotate) the feature is unusable — keep it operator-opt-in and document mkcert/openssl one-liners, or scope creep looms.
- Terminology drift: the issue text references channel_lan (renamed portal_net in 0.12.0, and #490 deletes the legacy network) and a stale #434; implementing against the issue text literally would target the wrong network/surface.
- Doc-drift test coupling: scripts/security-posture-doc-drift.test.ts asserts exact prose/code agreement for the guardian security posture; core-principles.md edits must be made in the same change or CI fails.
- Scope discipline: the seams are done and the issue explicitly forbids shipping additional identity providers — reviewers should reject any drift toward a richer authz engine; only Basic + mTLS transport identity belong in the public guardian.

## Original issue body

# #435: Guardian: mTLS adapter auth + keep authn/authz seams generic 

# Guardian: mTLS adapter auth + keep the authn/authz seams generic (public ships Basic only)

Public-repo scope for guardian auth: **keep authentication to the current Basic (OpenCode) model**, add **mTLS** for adapter transport identity, and keep the #429/#433 seams generic so additional providers can be supplied downstream — without the public guardian shipping them. The public guardian stays single-tenant with Basic auth.

> An extension of the 0.12.0 seams (#429/#433), not a re-architecture.

## Public authentication (current — unchanged)
- **Basic `channelId:channelSecret` → Principal** (#429) — the single credential/identity model, as today.
- Existing static **admin / MCP gateway bearer tokens** (`GUARDIAN_ADMIN_TOKEN_FILE`, `GUARDIAN_MCP_TOKEN_FILE`) — unchanged infra plumbing.

## New public strategy
- **mTLS client cert** — cryptographic **adapter transport identity** on the LAN (`channel_lan`). A machine/transport identity for adapters, not an identity provider. *(this issue owns it — no other issue tracks it; the stale #434 reference was wrong.)*

## Keep the seams generic (so providers can be supplied downstream)
- The #429 `authenticate(request) → Principal` step stays a **generic seam**; Basic + mTLS are the public strategies behind it.
- The gate (allowlist / ownership / bounds / rate / moderation, #429) stays the public authorization surface, and its policy decision is exposed as a **pluggable policy-provider seam** keyed on the generic `Principal` (#433).
- The public guardian ships **only the Basic policy** (the current gate). It does **not** add identity providers or a richer authorization-policy engine.

## Security invariants
- Default-deny gate; credentials/tokens never logged; guardian-only ingress, fail-closed moderation, loopback-default assistant — all unchanged.

## Out of public scope
Additional authentication **providers** and any richer authorization model are not part of the public guardian — only **Basic (+ mTLS)** ship here. The seams above exist precisely so such providers can be supplied downstream without forking the guardian.

## Dependencies / relationships
- **#429** (authn seam + gate), **#433** (`Principal` registry), **#22** (personas), **#432/#434** (standard-protocol ingress + portals).

---

<sub>Public scope: Basic (OpenCode) auth (current) + mTLS adapter transport identity, with generic authn/authz seams. Additional providers and richer authorization are out of public scope.</sub>
